title: A student tests a moving coil galvanometer
body: In the physics laboratory, Meera is given a moving coil galvanometer. Its rectangular coil has N turns, each of area A, and hangs between concave pole pieces with a cylindrical soft iron core at the centre, so that the coil always sees a radial magnetic field of strength B. When a current I flows, the magnetic torque NIAB turns the coil, and a spring with torsional constant k provides a restoring torque k phi. The pointer comes to rest at a deflection phi = (NAB/k) I. Meera's teacher defines the current sensitivity as phi/I and the voltage sensitivity as phi/V, where V = IR_G and R_G is the resistance of the coil. Meera now rewinds the coil using twice the length of the same wire, so that the number of turns doubles while the area of each turn, the field B and the spring are unchanged. The longer wire also doubles the resistance of the coil.
